inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 40.952M basic on the Q2-2026 10-Q cover (2026-07-27) + 0.29M incremental RSU/option shares (H1-2026 dilutive-securities line). The $1,437.5M convertible notes issued H1-2026 are carried as debt at face (not converted) - at the current price they are out of the money. Held FLAT: SBC (incl. withholding taxes) is fully expensed in the flows, so diluting the count too would double-charge it.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash-flow statement via SEC XBRL: ShareBasedCompensation $151.3M + AdjustmentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation $46.2M (Tyler publishes no combined figure, so the two lines are summed). H1-2026 run-rate: $80.8M + $28.0M = 8.6% of revenue.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD build. Risk-free ~4.3% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, levered beta ~0.9 for a mission-critical public-sector software vendor with ~87% recurring revenue -> cost of equity ~8.8-9.0%. Debt is ~3% of market cap (0.x% coupon converts) so WACC ~ cost of equity; 9.0% used in all three scenarios (risk charged once via scenarios, not via WACC).
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases (~$46M liability, ~$11M/yr cost) are small and their cost sits inside operating expenses, so inside the EBITDA margin; lease liabilities are NOT added to net debt (one treatment).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing: US operating SaaS/software company; no prior DCF, no memory entry - fresh build). FY0 = FY2025 actuals; the FY2026 growth year is anchored to guidance (revenue $2.535-2.575B, mid $2.555B = +9.5%, includes For The Record acquired April 2026 for $212.7M). Adjusted EBITDA margin is pre-SBC: FY2025 GAAP operating income $357.7M + D&A $138.4M + SBC $151.3M = $647.3M = 27.8% (H1-2026 27.8%). Reported FCF follows Tyler's own definition: OCF $653.5M - PP&E capex $16.0M - capitalized software $16.8M = $620.7M (26.6%). Owner FCF = 620.7 - 197.5 SBC incl. withholding - 34.9 interest income (other non-operating income $37.6M less $2.7M rental income) = $388.3M (16.6%). Interest income is stripped because the $1,015M liquid pile is added back in the bridge. ANCHORS: 2026-06-30 balance sheet - cash $895.4M + short-term investments $74.7M + long-term investments $45.2M = $1,015.3M liquid; debt = new convertible senior notes $1,437.5M face (carrying $1,408.7M; the $600M 2026 converts were repaid in March 2026). Net debt $422.2M. Caveat: the share count (2026-07-27) postdates the cash (2026-06-30), so any July buybacks lower the count without lowering the cash we credit - a small overstatement (each $100M of July buybacks ~ +$2/share). BUYBACKS: Tyler is a repurchaser - $174.7M FY2025, $755.0M in H1-2026 (funded by the new converts), new $1.5B authorization August 2026 - so the flat count is being funded, not merely assumed. Cash taxes have run far below book (FY2025 $40.8M paid on $390M pretax; H1-2026 $16.5M on $227M) because restored immediate R&D expensing (Section 174) lifted deferred taxes; the cash tax path ramps from 12% to 23% by year 5. Acquired-intangible amortisation (~$89M next year, falling to ~$57M by year 5 per the FY2025 10-K schedule) is why D&A glides from 5.6% toward a ~2% steady state, above capex (1.5%) only while that amortisation runs off.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_3yr_cagr (8.0%) cross-checked against FY2026 guidance (+9.5%) and the 2030 target of 10-12% organic recurring-revenue CAGR; equity CAGR rejected as the primary anchor
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 13.3% diverges >30% from EPS 5yr CAGR 8.5%, and equity is now shrinking ($3.70B FY2025 -> $3.04B Q2-2026) as $755M of H1-2026 buybacks are funded with convertible debt. The 5yr revenue CAGR (15.9%) is inflated by the NIC acquisition (2021). Book value is not a usable growth anchor for this business.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (OCF - capex - capitalized software - SBC - withholding taxes - interest income when net cash material): FY2020 $246.3M, FY2022 $201.2M, FY2024 $400.2M, FY2025 $388.3M. The 5yr owner-FCF CAGR (9.5%) is well below the 5yr reported-FCF CAGR (13.7%): SBC + withholding rose from $80M (FY2020) to $198M (FY2025), so a growing share of reported FCF growth is paid for in stock. The 3yr figures (24.5% owner, 23.3% reported) start from FY2022, a year depressed by Section 174 cash taxes, and overstate the run-rate.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 at guidance midpoint; then a haircut to the 2030 plan - total revenue ~$3.5B in 2030 vs ~$3.6-3.7B implied by management's $3.3-3.4B recurring target at >90% mix - fading to 3.5% by year 10.
base.ebitda_margin_rationale: Pre-SBC EBITDA runs ~2pp above Tyler's non-GAAP operating margin. Management's mid-30s non-GAAP operating margin by 2030 implies ~36-37% EBITDA; base reaches 33.2% in 2030 and 35.8% at maturity, i.e. lands the target 3-4 years late.

scenario_narratives.base: Tyler executes the cloud migration broadly on plan but slower than the June 2026 Investor Day targets: SaaS keeps growing high-teens to ~20% while on-premises maintenance runs off 5-7% a year, so total revenue compounds ~8.5% to 2030 (~$3.5B vs the ~$3.6-3.7B implied by management's recurring target) and then fades to 3.5%. The ~1.7x revenue uplift per flipped client and hosting-cost leverage (AWS) push pre-SBC EBITDA from 27.8% to ~33% by 2030 and ~36% at maturity. Agentic-AI products contribute from 2028 but are not a separate growth leg. SBC including withholding taxes eases only from 8.5% to 7% of revenue; cash taxes normalise from the Section-174-depressed ~10% to 23%.
scenario_narratives.bull: The 2030 plan is met or beaten: peak 'flips' in 2027-2029 land at the 85% migration target, AI monetisation starting H2-2027 adds an upsell layer on the 13,000-customer installed base, and transaction revenue grows low-teens once the Texas payments contract laps. Revenue compounds ~10% to 2030 (~$3.75B), pre-SBC EBITDA reaches the mid-30s non-GAAP operating margin target (~36% EBITDA) in 2030 and 39% at maturity, and SBC drifts down to 6.5% as the stock-heavy hiring phase of the cloud build ends.
scenario_narratives.bear: State and local budgets tighten (reduced federal transfers, a recession) and multi-year migration and new-logo projects slip; maintenance attrition runs ahead of SaaS conversion, lower-cost point solutions (OpenGov, BS&A, Edmunds) cap pricing in small municipalities, and AI monetisation proves a feature rather than a revenue line. Growth decelerates to ~5-6% after FY2026, EBITDA margin expansion stalls near 31%, SBC stays ~8% of revenue, and the incremental cyber risk on sensitive court/law-enforcement data adds cost. The business remains highly cash-generative and the franchise is intact - this is a de-rating case, not an impairment case.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% default): 100% concentration in U.S. state/local budgets and a five-year plan whose margin and AI legs are still ahead of proof (peak flips 2027-2029, AI monetisation H2-2027+). Base 50%: guidance has been met or raised through H1-2026 with record bookings. Bull 30% (below the 35% default): it needs migration, AI upsell and margin targets to all land together, and the base already credits most of management's 2030 margin target.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Tyler is a high-quality, low-churn public-sector software franchise mid-way through an on-premises-to-SaaS migration. The house valuation charges SBC plus net-share-settlement taxes in full (~8.5% of revenue) and strips interest income on the cash pile, and builds margins from components rather than carrying the FY2026 26-28% (street-basis) FCF margin forward. On that basis the value rests on whether management's 2030 margin target is delivered on time; the street (SBC-as-non-cash) basis sits much higher and is the regime most sell-side targets use.
key_risks_to_valuation: Margin path: ~60% of value is terminal, and the terminal margin is a ~8pp expansion from today - a two-year slip in the 2030 mid-30s operating-margin target moves base value materially
SBC treatment: SBC plus withholding is ~8.5% of revenue; the house/street band is wide and the price sits inside it
Convertible notes ($1.4375B) are treated as debt at face; a large share-price recovery above the conversion price would turn them into dilution instead
State/local budget cycle and federal-transfer cuts hit 100% of revenue at once
Cash-tax normalisation: the ~10% cash rate of FY2025-H1 2026 is a Section 174 timing benefit, not a permanent rate
